item.title: The Nancy Grace Roman Telescope begins its journey into deep space
item.description: NASA launched a telescope named after Nancy Grace Roman, the pioneering astronomer whose work helped make Hubble and generations of space telescopes possible.

item.title: Finally, an economic indicator you can eat
item.description: A corn dog may look like lunch. But to an economist, the price is a bigger story about food prices and inflation.

item.title: Getting aid to Nepal's flood survivors is the next challenge
item.description: The U.S. has pledged 3.5 million in flood aid for Tibet and Nepal, with the first $500,000 distributed by Catholic Relief Services. An aid worker with the group explains what flood survivors need now.

item.title: Insanity defenses rarely work. Lindsay Clancy's case may be different
item.description: Insanity defenses are notoriously difficult to win. But Massachusetts law could give Lindsay Clancy a better chance.

item.title: Noel Godin, who made powerful people nervous around cream pies, dies at 80
item.description: For more than 50 years, Noel Godin went after famous and powerful people with cream pies. His targets included politicians, philosophers, filmmakers and, famously, Bill Gates.

item.title: Cineplexity: When singers become movie stars
item.description: Dolly Parton built a movie career on top of an already huge music career. Other singers have tried, with mixed results.

item.title: What a Brazilian tradition can teach us about the future of psychedelics
item.description: Researchers are looking at new ways to use psychedelics to treat depression. Science journalist Marcelo Leite says there's also a lot to learn from indigenous people who have used them for generations.

item.title: The Ukrainian women disappearing into Russian prisons
item.description: What happens when Russia arrests civilians in the Ukrainian territories it occupies? New Yorker writer Joshua Yaffa followed a group of women through the Russian prison system.

item.title: He offered strangers $10 to tie his shoe. Then things got weird
item.description: Would $10 convince you to walk up to a stranger and tie their shoe? One Minneapolis artist turned that question into delightfully public chaos.

item.title: Trump says U.S. has struck a deal for control of Venezuelan oil reserves
item.description: President Trump says a new deal with Venezuela would give the U.S. control of more than 65 billion barrels of oil reserves.
